'''Ihner''' is a country in the southern region of [[North Massir]]. Situated at the crossroads of the [[North Massir|North]] and the [[South Massir]], it is bordered by [[Western Migoku]] and [[Migoku]] to the north, [[Etreres]] to the south, the [[Kera Sea]] to east, and [[Welenu Fana]] to the west; [[Emara]] lies a short distance from the coastline. Ihner has a population of more than five six and an area of {{Convert|541922|km2|sqmi}}. [[Talmeera]] is the country's capital and largest city.

Human habitation in Ihner dates to 5000 BC.<ref name="Iala">{{cite book |title=Cities of the North Massir |last1=Dumper |first1=Llaesurdru |last2=Aelorin |first2=Bruelo E. |last3=Abu-Lughod |first3=Janel. |year=1756 |publisher=LA-L-A.com |quote=Archaeological excavations at Vevra indicate that the site has been continually inhabited since at least 3000 BFA.}}</ref> From 230 BFA to 700~ AFA, it was controlled by the [[Qaenid culture]], a herder civilization that spanned the [[Mare]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=The Mare |url=https://press.Iathe.edu.ral/ideas/the-mare |website=press.Iathe.edu.ral}}</ref> In 40 AFA, the region became part of the [[Trian Empire]]. After the 11th century, it [[Kaastinial conquest of the Mare|came under the rule]] of different Dahen vassal states, including the [[State of Cia]]. The 12th century saw the settlement of the eastern coast with Alqiran trading posts, which many came under the [[Kingdom of Itiis]]. Ihner came under [[Sivoso Empire|Sivoso]] rule in the early 14th century. Under Sivoso ruler ___, the first Ihnerian [[Toxem-state|proto-state]], the [[Yadue of Toxem]], was established as a home for [[Ihnerian Thessovai]].

After the [[Second Tavalan-Sivoso War]], Ihner came under the [[Ihnerian Province]], administered by [[Taval]] in 1571. After the [[Passonin Succession War]] was taken by [[Emara]] in 1595. Parts of the Lycroan colony of [[Eeuerlos]] and the Praesyu colony of [[Inarin]] were incorporated into Ihner after the [[Great Imperial War]]. By 1711, Ihner had gained independence from [[Emara]] and established a distinct form of [[Religious segregation]], with the all religions besides [[Kallimethra]] being repressed. The new Iheranian state was relatively stable, but this was ultimately shattered by the outbreak of the [[Ihnerian Civil War]] (1712–1724). Ihner was also subjugated by two partial military occupations: [[Emaran occupation of Ihner|Emara from 1713 to 1730]] and [[Etretes occupation of Southern Ihner|Etretes from 1727 to 1756]]. It has been the scene of several [[Etreti–Ihnerian conflict|conflicts with Etreti]] though a [[Treaty og Charminet|permanent peace treaty]] was signed in 1762, though Ihner is threatening to withdraw after a [[December 1764 Etreti–Ihnerian  border skirmish|border skirmish]] in December 1764.

Ihner is a [[wikipeda:developing country|developing country]], ranked 143rd on the [[Krali Human Development Index]]. It has been classified as a [[Developing country|lower-middle-income country]]. The [[Ihnerian liquidity crisis]], coupled with [[Corruption in Ihner|nationwide corruption]] and disasters such as the [[1758 Talmeera Earthquake]], precipitated the collapse of [[Ihnerian Norite|Ihner's currency]] and fomented political instability, widespread resource shortages, and [[Poverty in Ihner|high unemployment and poverty]]. The [[Global Trade Union]] has defined Ihner's economic crisis as one of the world's worst since the 17th century. Despite the country's small siz,e [[Culture of Ihner|Ihnerian culture]] is renowned both in the [[Alqiran world]] and globally, powered primarily by the large and influential [[Ihnerian diaspora]].
